markdown_report:
The best next step is a position-preserving recency probe for the existing NextItNet adapter. At 10% research progress, trustworthy intervention measurements remain more feasible than architectural changes without supporting evidence.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Electronics has a 12.27% sampled negative-over-positive rate, versus 0.96% for CDs_and_Vinyl; this motivates investigation, not a validation-performance conclusion. (2) Deletion and compaction alter positions and convolutional context, confounding information removal. (3) Feedback motivates recency hypotheses, but ownership, compatibility and unmet needs remain unobserved.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [NextItNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163) expands structural coverage; reachability and path multiplicity can confound recency comparisons. (2) [Activation-patching research](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/06a52a54c8ee03cd86771136bc91eb1f-Abstract-Conference.html) and [replacement explanations](https://csr21.github.io/xu-csr2021.pdf) motivate corruption and plausibility controls; neither validates this adapter. (3) [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) distinguish sampled from catalog ranking; [cluster-bootstrap guidance](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7148287/) cautions against treating dependent prefixes as independent users.

**Framework and directions.** Organize intervention validity, mechanism localization and recommendation relevance by three evidence levels: training sensitivity, qualitative hypotheses and held-out performance. Cross intervention type—content replacement, order permutation, activation patching—with controls for accessibility, corruption severity and candidate competition. No current observation identifies a successful repair.

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means greater effort.

- **Matched lag replacements — 5/7/6.** Originality: useful task-specific integration; established method. Potential: guides focused repairs; synthetic sensitivity may not transfer. Difficulty: existing interfaces suffice; plausibility and competition controls complicate matching.
- **Residual-block activation recovery — 6/7/7.** Originality: adapts causal tracing; established technique. Potential: localizes computation; recovery does not establish necessity. Difficulty: hooks help; alignment and normalization remain delicate.
- **Evidence-backed relevance audit — 4/6/5.** Originality: links complaints to observable content; familiar rubric. Potential: separates topicality from specificity; sparse descriptions limit coverage. Difficulty: simple labels; credible evaluation needs independent annotation.

**Selected algorithm.** Sample fixed training prefixes; replace equal numbers of recent or older nonterminal items in place, preserving padding, positions and timestamps. Compare frequency-matched random and locally plausible replacements across predefined doses and repeated draws. Match reachability and displacement where possible; report unmatched strata and identity controls. Freeze targets and candidates. For context-only sampled probes, replacements must fall outside candidates. Full-catalog probes cannot satisfy this: additionally remove inserted items identically from both conditions and report that restricted-catalog estimand separately. Measure target scores, fixed-negative margins, exact chunked ranks, top-ten overlap and matching coverage. Average within users before user bootstrap; separate corruption Monte Carlo error. Small-user intervals remain exploratory.

Preserve `DiagnosisProbe`, `run_full_diagnosis`, the interpreter and ModelView interfaces; restore modes and RNG states, and use maximum nonpadding readout. Retain one NextItNet checkpoint/category and unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10 selection. Predeclare probes and limited repair hypotheses: diagnostic calibration and bootstrap intervals do not prevent adaptive validation overfitting.

idea.description: Strengthen the existing NextItNet adapter with position-preserving, plausibility-controlled lag replacements that separate context sensitivity from inserted-candidate competition and architectural accessibility.
idea.motivation: Deletion probes confound information removal with positional changes, while unrestricted replacements can create implausible histories or directly promote inserted candidate items. Supplied feedback motivates testing recency, but training margins, qualitative narratives and perturbation sensitivity do not establish generalization or identify an effective repair.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Use the actual view.model through item_emb, log2feats and predict_score; do not fit auxiliary predictors or combine recommendation scores. Keep the original family-specific sample_batch and ModelView contracts. Build frequencies and optional local transition-count neighborhoods exclusively from training histories; these neighborhoods select diagnostic corruptions only. Optional lexical similarity may use available titles/descriptions without downloaded weights. Missing content means unavailable evidence, not incompatibility. Specify prefix sampling, item-frequency bin edges, lag-band boundaries, replacement doses, draw counts, user counts and matching tolerances in a versioned protocol before inspecting effects. A feasible initial protocol samples up to 12 eligible training users/category, two prefixes/user, five corruption draws and doses of one and two replacements, reporting actual coverage; this diagnostic sample is separate from the required five simulator users/category. Use a dedicated seed-42 generator and deterministic prefix ordering. Keep timestamps, sequence length, padding, occupied positions and the terminal item fixed. Exclude padding, target, original-prefix items and duplicate replacements from pools. Compare frequency-matched random replacements with replacements additionally matched on local transition or lexical similarity; record pool sizes and matching failures without silently relaxing rules. Use equal position counts and matched frequency distributions across lag bands; measure embedding displacement and architectural reachability/path-count differences, stratifying where common support exists. Enumerate convolutional taps and residual paths only when the actual implementation supports exact accounting; gates, global summaries or position-dependent operations must be included or reported as preventing exact characterization. Structural path counts do not measure learned influence. Preserve previous permutation probes as separate order-sensitivity tests with the selected item multiset unchanged. Freeze the target, candidate identities/order and original-prefix eligibility for each paired comparison. A sampled context-only probe can exclude all candidates from replacement pools; do not request or reconstruct hidden validation data. For full eligible-catalog probes, inserted unseen items necessarily overlap candidates: report original fixed-catalog effects and a separate paired comparison removing the same inserted IDs from both clean and altered candidate sets. Label the latter restricted-catalog ranks rather than full-catalog ranks. Report inserted-item score/rank gains separately; neither this decomposition nor target-score changes identify causal user intent. Count greater scores in catalog chunks and break exact ties by ascending item ID, with padding excluded. Use maximum nonpadding readout, never count-1; skip all-padding inputs. Include identity/no-op controls, a synthetic chunk/tie check, causal-isolation checks and unreachable-position controls only where structurally valid. Retain all original embedding and sampled-margin diagnostics, describing cosine alignment without claiming collapse from alignment alone. Average paired effects across prefixes/draws within user, then resample users within category; macro-average category effects equally only when all categories are measured. Report category effects, sample counts, corruption Monte Carlo error and exploratory user-bootstrap intervals; use null intervals for fewer than two users. Few users remain inadequate for strong uncertainty claims, and more corruption draws do not increase independent user counts. Calibration faults and dose sweeps test false alarms and sensitivity; do not assume monotonicity or confidence-interval coverage without a specified reference effect. Restore individual module modes and Python, NumPy, CPU and CUDA RNG states in finally. Return metrics, definitions, denominators, protocol, coverage, architecture checks, paired observations, strata, cost and unavailable-data reasons. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches/epoch, single GPU, all four routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, checkpoint/predictor consistency and the pinned evaluator. This revision changes diagnostics only, requiring no predictor architecture change. Retain full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five real training users/category. Predeclare a small repair hypothesis set, log every trial and cost, and use only host macro validation HR@10 for selection; no other checkpoints or hidden test files may be read.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        saved = capture_module_modes_and_rng_states(self.view.model)
        try:
            rng = dedicated_generator(seed=42)
            self.view.model.eval()
            with torch.no_grad():
                protocol = frozen_protocol()
                baseline_metrics = existing_family_aware_probes(train_loader)
                prefixes = fixed_training_prefix_sample(self.view.user_train, protocol)
                pools = training_only_frequency_and_local_neighborhoods(self.view)
                architecture = inspect_actual_temporal_dependencies(self.view.model)
                records = []
                for category, user, sequence, target in prefixes:
                    if not sequence.ne(0).any():
                        record_skip('all_padding')
                        continue
                    candidates = frozen_original_prefix_eligibility(sequence, target)
                    clean = measure(self.view, sequence, target, candidates,
                                    readout='maximum_nonpadding_index',
                                    rank='chunked_score_then_item_id')
                    bands = matched_lag_positions(sequence, architecture,
                                                  keep_terminal=True)
                    for dose, draw, replacement_type in protocol.conditions:
                        plans = paired_replacement_plans(
                            sequence, target, bands, pools, rng,
                            dose=dose, replacement_type=replacement_type)
                        for plan in plans:
                            if not plan.matches_protocol:
                                record_matching_failure(plan)
                                continue
                            altered = replace_items_in_place(sequence, plan)
                            changed = measure(self.view, altered, target, candidates)
                            inserted = set(plan.replacement_ids)
                            restricted = candidates.without(inserted)
                            clean_restricted = measure(self.view, sequence, target, restricted)
                            changed_restricted = measure(self.view, altered, target, restricted)
                            records.append(paired_record(
                                category, user, clean, changed,
                                clean_restricted, changed_restricted,
                                inserted_item_effects=True, matching=plan.metadata))
                controls = identity_causality_chunking_and_applicable_reachability_checks()
                metrics = aggregate_within_user_then_bootstrap_within_category(records)
                metrics.update(separate_corruption_monte_carlo_error(records))
                metrics.update(baseline_metrics)
                return {'metrics': attach_protocol_coverage_controls_and_cost(metrics, controls),
                        'metric_definitions': definitions_with_estimands_counts_and_limitations()}
        finally:
            restore_module_modes_and_rng_states(saved)

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return grounded_prompt(
        raw_diagnosis,
        distinguish_training_sensitivity_from_generalization=True,
        distinguish_fixed_catalog_from_restricted_catalog=True,
        require_measured_evidence_and_report_failed_matching=True,
        prohibit_unobserved_traits_and_unsupported_causal_claims=True,
        preserve_nextitnet_and_single_model_constraint=True)

originality.positive: Integrates lag matching, plausibility, architectural accessibility and candidate-competition controls into a concrete NextItNet diagnostic protocol.
originality.negative: Replacement interventions, paired ranking measurements and cluster resampling are established techniques; the contribution is methodological integration.

future_potential.positive: Could help allocate limited training budget to context-use hypotheses supported by reproducible measurements.
future_potential.negative: Training-prefix sensitivity and synthetic corruption plausibility may not predict held-out improvements, and small diagnostic samples limit conclusions.

code_difficulty.positive: Existing scoring interfaces support implementation without changing or retraining the deployed architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Plausibility matching, architecture-dependent reachability, candidate-overlap decomposition and separate uncertainty components require substantial care.

related_work.title: NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Uses residual dilated causal convolutions for sequential recommendation.
Provides the backbone whose context sensitivity the proposed probes measure.
limitations: Structural receptive-field coverage does not establish which interactions determine a prediction.
Exact reachable lags require tracing actual convolutional taps, residual paths and any additional context mechanisms.

related_work.title: ICLR 2024 activation-patching research supplied in the search results
contributions: Supports controlling corruption methods and measurement choices when interpreting intervention results.
limitations: Does not establish the validity of these proposed NextItNet interventions.
Activation recovery does not by itself establish necessity or a useful model repair.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation can distort comparisons between recommendation models.
limitations: Does not justify replacing the pinned sampled validation metric with catalog-wide diagnostics.

related_work.title: Uncertainty in Online Experiments with Dependent Data
contributions: Motivates accounting for dependence when estimating uncertainty.
Supports retaining a user's paired observations together during resampling.
limitations: User bootstrap intervals do not capture training-seed variability, all item dependence or adaptive validation-selection bias.

related_work.title: Learning Causal Explanations for Recommendation
contributions: Provides precedent for fixed-length replacement histories sampled through a learned history distribution.
Motivates considering replacement plausibility alongside intervention size.
limitations: The proposed training-count or lexical matching scheme does not reproduce its learned history distribution.
Plausible replacements alone do not identify causal preference or validate recency repairs.

related_work.title: CETD study supplied in the search results
contributions: Motivates respecting temporal dependencies and proximity to original histories when constructing interventions.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed NextItNet diagnostic protocol or its plausibility thresholds.

related_work.title: Substitution-Based Profile Pollution study supplied in the search results
contributions: Provides related use of neighborhood-based item substitutions.
limitations: Substitution attacks and defenses pursue different objectives from measuring useful context dependence.

related_work.title: Understanding the Effective Receptive Field in Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
contributions: Distinguishes theoretical receptive-field extent from effective influence.
limitations: Its general CNN results should not be assumed to characterize a particular causal NextItNet implementation.

related_work.title: ClusterBootstrap guidance supplied in the search results
contributions: Supports cluster-level resampling when observations within a user are dependent.
Motivates caution with few independent clusters.
limitations: Does not make intervals reliable with only five users per category or correct adaptive model selection.

related_work.title: Monte Carlo error assessment guidance supplied in the search results
contributions: Motivates reporting stochastic simulation error separately from sampling uncertainty.
limitations: Additional corruption draws reduce simulation noise without increasing the number of independent users.

related_work.title: Benchmarking Neural Network Robustness to Common Corruptions and Perturbations
contributions: Provides precedent for controlled corruption types and severity sweeps.
limitations: Does not establish that recommendation diagnostic effects should vary monotonically with corruption dose.

related_work.title: Using Simulation Studies to Evaluate Statistical Methods
contributions: Supports explicit generating processes, reference effects and Monte Carlo error reporting when calibrating diagnostics.
limitations: Known injected fault severity alone does not provide a known diagnostic effect or establish confidence-interval coverage.
